mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances following a UNRATE increase > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the last two months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the housing sector and related industries experience growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances following a sustained increase in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the last two months signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as production slowdowns ripple through the economy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances following a significant decrease in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances following a significant increase in PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% over the last month, it signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending drives economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances following a significant increase in RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) both increase by more than 0.5% within the last month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the cost of capital rises and purchasing power decreases.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances following a joint increase in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) both show a decline of more than 1% over the last quarter, it signals a weakening demand side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth slows.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decrease > 1% in 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances following a joint decline in GDPC1 and HOUST.
